pll1d14c1-d1e3477.summary: Distinguishes the twofold procession of the Spirit: eternal and ineffable, from Father and Son without time; and temporal, from both to sanctify the creature. As eternally, so in time he proceeds jointly from both, not from the Father into the Son and from the Son to the creature.
claims: The Spirit's procession is twofold: eternal and temporal.
The temporal procession is for the sanctification of creatures.
In both, the Spirit proceeds jointly from Father and Son.

pll1d14c1-d1e3480.summary: Confirms with De Trinitate XV: the Spirit does not proceed from the Father into the Son and from the Son to sanctify the creature, but from both at once, though the Father gave the Son that he proceed from him.
claims: The Spirit does not proceed in sequence from Father to Son to creature.
The Spirit proceeds simultaneously from both.

pll1d14c1-d1e3498.summary: Cites Bede on the temporal procession: when the Spirit's grace is given to men, the Spirit is sent and proceeds from the Father and the Son, for his mission is his procession.
claims: The Spirit's mission is his temporal procession.
The Spirit is sent by Father and Son when his grace is given.

pll1d14c1-d1e3514.summary: Interprets Bede: the giving of the Spirit's grace is called his procession or mission, and since giving is only temporal, this procession is temporal.
claims: The giving of the Spirit is his procession or mission.

pll1d14c1-d1e3517.summary: Cites De Trinitate XV: after the resurrection Christ breathed on the disciples saying 'Receive the Holy Spirit' to show that the Spirit proceeds from him also; and the Spirit is the power that went out from him and healed all (Luke 6:19).
claims: Christ's breathing showed the Spirit proceeds from him.
The power that went out from Christ and healed is the Spirit.

pll1d14c1-d1e3554.summary: Adds Augustine to show that this procession is the giving of the Spirit: after the resurrection Christ gave the Spirit twice, on earth for love of neighbor and from heaven for love of God, since through this Gift charity is poured into our hearts (Rom 5:5).
claims: Christ gave the Spirit twice after the resurrection.
The earthly giving is for love of neighbor, the heavenly for love of God.
Through the Gift charity is poured into our hearts.

pl-l1d14c1.summary: Distinguishes the Spirit's twofold procession: eternal, from Father and Son ineffably and without time, and temporal, from both to sanctify the creature. In both, he proceeds from the two together, not from the Father to the Son and then from the Son to creatures (Augustine). Bede identifies the temporal procession with the sending and the giving of the Spirit's grace. Augustine sees it in Christ's breathing on the disciples and in the power that went out from him, and in the two givings after the resurrection, on earth for love of neighbor and from heaven for love of God, through which charity is poured into our hearts.
claims: The Holy Spirit has an eternal procession and a temporal procession.
In both, the Spirit proceeds from Father and Son jointly, not successively.
The temporal procession is the Spirit's mission and giving to sanctify the creature.
The Spirit's temporal procession is shown in Christ's breathing on the disciples.
Christ gave the Spirit twice after the resurrection: on earth for love of neighbor, from heaven for love of God.
